Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?
Target paper title: Adapting Visual-Language Models for Generalizable Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
Target paper abstract: Recent advancements in large-scale visual-language pre-trained models have led to significant progress in zero-/few-shot anomaly detection within natural image domains. However, the substantial domain divergence between natural and medical images limits the effectiveness of these methodologies in medical anomaly detection. This paper introduces a novel lightweight multi-level adaptation and comparison framework to repurpose the CLIP model for medical anomaly detection. Our approach integrates multiple residual adapters into the pre-trained visual encoder, enabling a stepwise enhancement of visual features across different levels. This multi-level adaptation is guided by multi-level, pixel-wise visual-language feature alignment loss functions, which recalibrate the model's focus from object semantics in natural imagery to anomaly identification in medical images. The adapted features exhibit improved generalization across various medical data types, even in zero-shot scenarios where the model encounters unseen medical modalities and anatomical regions during training. Our experiments on medical anomaly detection benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art models, with an average AUC improvement of 6.24% and 7.33% for anomaly classification, 2.03% and 2.37% for anomaly segmentation, under the zero-shot and few-shot settings, respectively. Source code is available at: https://github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD
Verified facts about the target paper's code: Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):

- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.

- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

The research idea:
TITLE: Size-constrained training of MVFA's segmentation branch from image-level labels
SUMMARY: Train the segmentation adapters with image-level labels and an inequality constraint on the predicted anomalous area of each image (zero for normal images, within a dataset-specific range for abnormal ones), without pixel-wise pseudo-masks.
HYPOTHESIS: Size-constrained training with area bounds estimated from label-restricted pseudo-mask statistics recovers at least 85% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities and matches pixel-wise pseudo-mask training within 2 points, while being insensitive (less than 1 point change) to a 2x error in the area bounds.
RATIONALE: Self-training improves pixel targets iteratively. By analogy with constrained weakly supervised segmentation (size-constrained CNN losses), the segmentation branch can instead be supervised at the level where labels are reliable, the image, plus a weak but robust prior on how much of an abnormal image is lesion. This avoids committing to any pixel-wise pseudo-mask and its boundary errors, and it directly asks what image-level labels alone can teach MVFA's segmentation adapters, which is the core of the problem.
METHOD: 1) Area bounds per source dataset: a_min, a_max = 10th and 90th percentiles of label-restricted pseudo-mask areas on abnormal training images. 2) Predicted area A = mean_x sigmoid(map(x)) on the seg branch output. 3) Loss for abnormal images: relu(a_min - A)^2 + relu(A - a_max)^2 plus a top-k MIL term -log mean of top-1% sigmoid(map); for normal images: A^2 plus the max-pixel BCE toward 0. 4) train_zero.py: replace Focal + Dice for pseudo-labelled datasets with this loss, weight 1; det branch unchanged. 5) Sensitivity: multiply a_min, a_max by 0.5 and 2. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; pixel-wise pseudo-masks; size-constrained loss; size-constrained with perturbed bounds. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if size-constrained training recovers less than 75% of the mask-supervised gain or changes by more than 2 points under a 2x bound error.
